# From efficiency to exposure {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Designed for cost, exposed to power

::::: columns

:::: {.column width="50%"}

### 1990–2015

- single sourcing
- just-in-time inventories
- production where cheapest
- premise: **trade stays apolitical**

::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}

### Since

- blocs (S04)
- sanctions (S10)
- **inputs** — today

::::

:::::

::: {.get}
Batteries, magnets, solar, wind, chips: **lithium · cobalt · nickel · graphite · rare earths · gallium · germanium**. Mining is concentrated. **Refining** is more so.
:::

# Three ways commodities become geopolitical {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Conflict · nationalism · control

| | Driver | Example | Actor |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Conflict commodities** | resources fund or motivate conflict | 3TG from eastern DRC | armed groups → smelters → buyers |
| **Resource nationalism** | capture more of the value | Indonesia's nickel-ore export bans (2014; again from 2020) | the producing state |
| **Strategic export controls** | coerce, signal, protect | China: gallium and germanium (2023), graphite (2023), rare earths (2025) | the dominant refiner |

::: {.warn}
**Cobalt** sits in all three rows: labour and conflict at the mine, quotas at the border, refining in China.
:::

## Le Billon & Shykora (2020)

> Supply chains are not pipes. They are **sites** where conflict, environmental harm and power are produced and passed on.

- Due diligence regimes — **OECD Guidance**, **Dodd–Frank §1502**, **EU Conflict Minerals Regulation** — move responsibility onto the importer
- They cover few minerals, audit the **smelter** rather than the mine
- They can lead firms to **avoid** a region rather than improve it

::: {.muted}
In S. O'Lear (Ed.), *A Research Agenda for Environmental Geopolitics*, pp. 59–73.
:::

# Weaponised interdependence {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Networks have hubs

**Farrell & Newman (2019):** global networks are **hub-and-spoke**, not flat. A state with jurisdiction over a hub can exploit

::::: columns

:::: {.column width="50%"}

### The panopticon

**See** what passes through: who pays whom, who ships what

::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}

### The chokepoint

**Deny** others access to the hub

::::

:::::

::: {.get}
Built on SWIFT and the dollar (S10). For minerals, **the refinery is the hub**.
:::

## Two conditions

1. The network is **concentrated** → measurable today, with the HHI
2. The state can **direct the firms** that run the hub → measurable in S12, with governance indicators

::: {.step}
A licence that is always granted is a **panopticon** before it is a **chokepoint**: the state now sees every shipment.
:::

# Export restrictions: the evidence {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Kowalski & Legendre (2023)

**The OECD inventory:** country × commodity × year since 2009 — export taxes, quotas, prohibitions, licensing, minimum export prices

- Restrictions on critical raw materials **multiplied several-fold** after 2009 — about fivefold in the 2023 paper
- Concentrated among a few **large producers**
- Concentrated in the **most concentrated** minerals

::: {.muted}
*OECD Trade Policy Papers* 269 · [doi:10.1787/c6bb598b-en](https://doi.org/10.1787/c6bb598b-en) · now the *Inventory of Export Restrictions on Critical Raw Materials* (2026 edition)
:::

## What the count does not measure

::: {.warn}
A **ban** and a **licence** each count once. A **5%** tax and a **40%** tax each count once.
:::

> **Put it to the room:** what would you need to know before telling a buyer that supply is at risk?

::: {.fragment}
Stringency · enforcement · the share of world supply covered · substitutes · stocks
:::

# Concentration, measured: the HHI {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## The Herfindahl–Hirschman index

$$
\text{HHI} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} s_i^2 \qquad s_i \text{ in percent}, \quad 0 < \text{HHI} \le 10\,000
$$

| Market | HHI |
|---|---|
| One producer, 100% | 10,000 |
| 70% · 20% · 10% | 4,900 + 400 + 100 = **5,400** |
| Ten equal producers | 1,000 |

::: {.step}
"Highly concentrated" above **2,500** — or **1,800** under the 2023 US Merger Guidelines.
:::

## The numbers equivalent

$$
N^{*} = \frac{1}{\sum_i s_i^2} \qquad s_i \text{ as fractions}
$$

- HHI 5,400 → $N^{*} \approx 1.9$ — "as concentrated as **two** equal producers"
- The figure a board understands

## Three decisions move the number

| Decision | Options | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Stage** | mine · refinery · exports | refining is usually far more concentrated |
| **"Other countries"** | one producer · dropped | inflates · deflates the denominator |
| **Units** | within one mineral | never pool minerals |

::: {.warn}
The USGS tables you transcribed are **mine** production. The chokepoint is usually at the **refinery**.
:::

# The system-wide signal: GSCPI {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Global Supply Chain Pressure Index

- New York Fed · monthly since 1997 · in **standard deviations** from average
- Transport costs + supply-chain components of manufacturing surveys
- Pandemic spike; eased in 2023

::: {.warn}
**Every release re-estimates the history.** The CSV has one column per vintage. Use one, and name it.
:::

::: {.muted}
System-wide: it says nothing about one mineral. It is the background, not the signal.
:::

# What can the firm do? {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## Six strategies

| Strategy | Cost | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| **Stockpile** | working capital | buys time, not supply |
| **Diversify** | price, qualification time | refinery may be in the same country |
| **Friend-shore** | premium, fewer suppliers | allied output may not exist yet |
| **Substitute** | R&D, performance | new chokepoints |
| **Integrate** | capital | swaps geopolitical for political risk |
| **Recycle** | scale, collection | small share for a decade |

::: {.get}
**Which two would your team's firm use?**
:::

## States are moving too

- **De-risking**, not decoupling — European Commission, 2023
- **EU Critical Raw Materials Act (2024)** — 2030 benchmarks: 10% extracted · 40% processed · 25% recycled in the EU · no more than **65%** from one third country
- Critical-mineral conditions on US EV tax credits

::: {.warn}
Each is a response to risk — and a new source of **regulatory** risk for the firm.
:::

# The Tableau skill of the day {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

## HHI, treemap, action

```text
Share  =  [Production] / {FIXED [Mineral] : SUM([Production])}
HHI    =  SUM( POWER([Share] * 100, 2) )          // Mineral on the view
```

1. **Treemap:** Country → Detail + Label · Production → Size · Share → Colour
2. **Dashboard:** treemap + restrictions chart + GSCPI
3. **Action:** *Dashboard → Actions → Filter* · source treemap · target restrictions · field Mineral

::: {.check}
Click a mineral; the restrictions chart follows. That is the interaction your team dashboard needs.
:::
